name: Madagascar Sparrowhawk
rangeDescription: Scrub and savanna of madagascar (except central)
description: Typical medium-sized sparrowhawk. Adults are gray on the back with fine gray barring below; females much larger.

name: Shaft-tailed Whydah
rangeDescription: Southern angola to namibia, zambia, botswana, southern mozambique, and kwazulu-natal
description: A small whydah with a reddish-orange bill and legs. The breeding male has buffy-orange underparts and neck, a dark cap, and 17-centimeter-long black tail feathers.

name: Subdesert Mesite
rangeDescription: Coastal subdesert of southwestern madagascar
description: Odd ground-dwelling bird that is rarely seen by those not looking for it. Males have pale underparts with dark spots, while females have heavy reddish markings below.

name: Hispaniolan Spindalis
rangeDescription: Hispaniola including gonâve
description: A somewhat small woodland bird that moves rather deliberately as it feeds on fruits and flowers and the occasional insect. Occupies wide range of forests from pines to mangroves.

name: Malaita Owl
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A rather small dark brown owl with black eyes, a white throat, and white eyebrows. Underparts are densely barred.

name: Great Xenops
rangeDescription: Arid caatinga of interior northeastern and east-central brazil
description: Large and subtly beautiful xenops with a pointy curved bill. Has bright rusty plumage with a white throat.

name: Malayan Crested Argus
rangeDescription: Mountains of central malay peninsula (taman negara national park)
description: A large brown pheasant of low hill forest, as well as the transition zone from lowland to hill forest. Shy and extremely difficult to see, and highly restricted in range.

name: Sombre Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Halmahera (northern moluccas)
description: A large forest kingfisher with a dark back, white underparts, and a white eyebrow and collar. Back color is earth-brown in females and tinged with green in males.

name: Ecuadorian Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern ecuador (azuay and el oro)
description: Rare and endangered tapaculo found only in a small area of wet foothill rainforest in the Andes of southwestern Ecuador. Plumage is mostly gray with a brown belly that has dark barring.

name: Gray-fronted Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Cuba (rare)
description: A multicolored chunky dove of dense, wet forests with thick leaf-litter. It is most often found on the ground, sometimes in association with Blue-headed or Ruddy Quail-Doves.

name: Caracas Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of northern venezuela (aragua, miranda, and distrito federal)
description: Boldly patterned sparrow with black head and white eyebrow. Back and tail olive-yellow, underparts white; black band across chest.

name: Long-tailed Paradigalla
rangeDescription: Western new guinea (arfak and fakfak mountains)
description: A large, fairly long-tailed bird of montane forest on the Bird’s Head of New Guinea. All black plumage with iridescence on the head, fairly long bill, distinctive, yellow wattle between the eye and the bill.

name: Sulawesi Brown Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sulawesi foothill forest
description: A recently described streak-throated brown flycatcher. Gray-brown above and pale whitish below with broad breast streaks and a dirty throat.

name: Banggai Golden-Bulbul
rangeDescription: Peleng, banggai, and labobo, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A noticeably long-billed thrush-sized bird with an olive head and upperside and uniform yellow underparts. Pairs or small groups inhabit forests, edges, and plantations in the lowlands and foothills.

name: White-bellied Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (junín, lima, and huancavelica)
description: Striking, critically endangered bird found only at extremely high elevations in the Andes of central Peru. One of the most beautiful members of the ovenbird family, with immaculate white underparts and wing patches contrasting with its deep chestnut upperparts and gray crown.

name: New Ireland Myzomela
rangeDescription: New ireland (northeastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A tiny curve-billed myzomela. Male is red-faced with olive-green upperparts and buffy cream underparts.

name: Spot-winged Starling
rangeDescription: Foothills of northern india and nepal; winters to myanmar and thailand
description: Uncommon pale-eyed starling with a white patch on each wing. Male is metallic dark blue-gray above with an orange breast and belly.

name: Sao Tome Short-tail
rangeDescription: Locally in forest of southern são tomé
description: A dull, short-tailed brownish forest-floor skulker, cold above and warmer below. Has a very thin beak, and long legs and big feet that it lifts in a “goosestep” fashion.

name: White-winged Potoo
rangeDescription: Northern amazonia (northeastern peru and northern brazil) and eastern brazil (bahia and espírito santo)
description: Uncommon, rarely seen potoo, active only at night. If found during the day, large white wing patches are key to identification.

name: Tumbes Pewee
rangeDescription: Andes of western ecuador and western peru (southward to ica)
description: Small flycatcher found in dry and semi-humid forest in western Ecuador and western Peru. It is mostly gray with pale wingbars and a small crest.
